hooks.text: Astronauts floating in orbit are actually not beyond Earth's gravity.
Earth's gravity at the space station is nearly 90 percent strong.
Weightlessness in orbit is just a state of constant free fall.

title: Gravity in Space Is Stronger Than You Think
description: Discover why astronauts float in orbit even though Earth's gravity is still nearly 90 percent as strong at the space station.

beats.text: Astronauts floating in orbit are actually not beyond Earth's gravity.
beats.visual: photograph of the International Space Station orbiting Earth, NASA, 2021

beats.text: While many believe space is a complete zero gravity vacuum, the everyday reality is quite different.
beats.visual: diagram of Earth gravity and orbital altitude comparison

beats.text: At the soaring altitude of the space station, Earth's gravitational field is still nearly 90 percent as strong as on the ground.
beats.visual: diagram of Earth gravity decrease with altitude

beats.text: Human space travellers do not float because gravity has vanished entirely from their location.
beats.visual: photograph of astronaut floating inside the International Space Station, NASA, 2018

beats.text: Instead, they stay up because they are caught in a continuous state of perpetual free fall.
beats.visual: illustration of Newton cannonball orbital mechanics thought experiment

beats.text: Their immense horizontal speed continually carries them around the curving horizon of our home planet.
beats.visual: diagram of satellite orbit trajectory around Earth

beats.text: That precise physics mechanism is why astronauts floating in orbit are actually not beyond Earth's gravity.
beats.visual: photograph of Earth curvature from the International Space Station, NASA, 2020
